requirement.summary: Events use authenticated creation, exact responses, case-insensitive search, stable ordering, and opaque cursor pagination.
A valid hold reserves all requested capacity once and every failed request is atomic.
Confirm and release are stable terminal operations, orders are unique, and histories are durable and sorted.
Pending holds expire without traffic and restore capacity once within two seconds of their deadline.
Sold-out customers can join, query, withdraw, and be promoted through the three published waitlist routes.
Two independent processes sharing PostgreSQL cannot oversell a contended event.
Mutation results and effects replay durably in operation/resource scope across disconnect and restart.
Confirm, release, and expiration have exactly one terminal winner and one capacity effect.
Waitlist promotion uses joinedAt then ID order, never bypasses an unsatisfied head, and promotes a fitting prefix.
Concurrent promotion and withdrawal across two processes never duplicate a promoted hold or oversell.
A completed hold response implies a durable reservation and replayable result visible from another process.
A replacement process expires a persisted hold at its original deadline without read-triggered business work.
Unknown confirm and release outcomes replay atomically without duplicate order or restoration.
Promotion converges to the same FIFO prefix after a process exits during the public release flow.
The production browser UI completes event browse, hold, confirm, history, and order flows accessibly.
The production UI reflects server-authoritative release and expiry state and recovers a known hold after refresh.
The production UI exposes join, position, withdraw, promotion countdown, and confirmation for a known customer and event.
OpenAPI 3.1 and runtime agree on every published route, closed success shape, input rule, and safe error envelope.
FINAL imports the literal V1 seed schema at scale and rejects invalid input atomically.
Event reads over the published large dataset meet the 250 ms p95 target with exact results.
One hundred concurrent clients meet the 500 ms hold/confirm p95 target without correctness anomalies.
The mixed public workload sustains 150 completed requests per second and preserves capacity and waitlist invariants.
